m.s: Fried rice works best with cold rice. If you didn't cook it yesterday, rinse {rice} and cook it with 1½ times its volume of water, covered on low for 12 minutes. Spread it on a tray and pop it in the fridge for at least an hour.

Thinly slice {chk_thigh} into small pieces and toss with a splash of the soy. Finely dice {carrot}, crush {garlic} and grate {ginger}. Slice {springonion}, keeping the whites and greens separate. Beat {eggs} with a pinch of salt.

Heat a drizzle of oil in a wok or large frying pan over high heat until smoking. Stir-fry the chicken for 4 to 5 minutes until cooked through, then set aside. Add a little more oil, pour in the eggs and scramble softly for 1 minute. Set aside with the chicken.
Add another drizzle of oil and stir-fry the carrot for 2 minutes. Add the garlic, ginger and spring onion whites and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.

Add the cold rice and break up any clumps. Press it flat into the wok and leave it for 1 minute to toast before tossing. Repeat three or four times. That's where the smoky fried rice flavour comes from.
Add {peas}, the chicken and egg, {soy} and {oyster}. Toss over high heat for 2 minutes until everything is piping hot. Finish with {sesameoil} and the spring onion greens.

l: Built for lunch. Reheat until piping hot all the way through. Keeps 3 days in the fridge.
g: Make the whole batch with tamari, and use a GF oyster sauce or skip it. Rice dishes are where hidden gluten sneaks in.
